subject.title: Feature: Built-in pace-aware rate limiting for autonomous agents

question: Should OpenClaw core own pace-aware provider quota enforcement for autonomous agents, and should the first implementation be visibility-only or opt-in throttling?
rationale: The proposal changes core runtime policy, provider usage semantics, subagent behavior, and config defaults; automation cannot choose the right product boundary or upgrade behavior safely.

options.title: Visibility-Only First
options.body: Reuse provider usage snapshots to expose pace/status context without blocking existing autonomous runs.

options.title: Opt-In Core Throttling
options.body: Add a new pace policy config with explicit thresholds, docs, schema, upgrade proof, and tests for both disabled/default and enabled behavior.

options.title: Keep Throttling External
options.body: Leave automatic enforcement to a skill/plugin or operator workflow unless a missing core extension point is identified.

recommendation.title: Visibility-Only First
recommendation.body: Reuse provider usage snapshots to expose pace/status context without blocking existing autonomous runs.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the clearest recent history on the provider usage and status paths that a visibility-first implementation would reuse.
